Leah: At Saturday's beginner workshop I put two ordinary practice notebooks on the table. Both had split cover cloth.
Leah: One opened freely. On the other, the cover pulled against the first page when I opened it.
Leah: I asked everyone to watch the hinge move before choosing where to add anything. The two covers looked similar while closed.
Leah: I photographed both books halfway through, with the old cloth exposed. Those photos show the different hinge positions much more clearly than the finished covers.
Visitor: When I switched my own craft business to before-and-after photos, my sales doubled.
Leah: I have not checked that visitor's result. I did not run their business or measure the effect of my workshop photos.
Leah: My notes for each practice repair now have three fields: what moves, what catches, and what I tried. I can reconstruct the decision from that page later.
Leah: A participant wanted to start on an old family book. I asked them to practice on scrap materials and ordinary notebooks first. Valuable or historic books are outside this beginner workshop.
Leah: For a short video I can film the two ordinary sample books opening side by side, point to the hinge, then show the three-field note. I have not filmed that clip yet.
